value.rationale: Different shore-specific contact requirements are a natural heterogeneity mechanism. The same five-vertex graph supports two primitive-four orbits under thresholds (1,1,2), but none under either uniform threshold one or two; the period-four mode is then destroyed by enlarging either sensitive shore, despite arbitrary size of the resistant shore. This robust size-isolation is a motivated qualitative boundary not just a narrow numerical table. The sharp seven-step global cutoff and all-size coefficient census add substantive complete dynamical information. Finite computer proof and priority risks are disclosed.
